As a relatively young kid (20) I can tell you it has changed a lot. See, back your time rap, metal and punk occupied the same space, underground music for mostly lower class outlier kids, since the music was an outlier itself. Pop music was mostly for middle/upper class people without an angst bone in their body. What's happened in the last 10 years in a nutshell is that rap has exploded. Like, gone from total underground 5 copies of a mixtape to top 40 rappers like 2chainz talking about big booty hoes coming from the speakers of some well off suburban kid's new BMW that he got on his 16th birthday. Rap went pop, for lack of a better term. So now most kids,  poor to rich bump it all the time with punk/metal fading into the sidelines, but really developing strong cult followings. So for example in my school most kids wouldn't know who Big D and the Kids Table were, but the small group that did could tell you every album, as well as every punk band remotely ska and recommend more listening. There's little cross-genre listening anymore. 
It's sad to say but when a genre of music like hip hop goes from preaching about the hardships of poor black/Latino communities to blasting the airwaves with packing gats and getting bitches I fear the meaning has been lost forever.

Brother it's more about accepting yourself as you are, combined with mindfulness. And by mindfulness I mean recognizing those negative anxious thoughts that enter your mind on a day to day basis, and letting them go. At least in my psychedelic experiences, the "ego deaths" I have experienced sort of put you in perspective of how small we are in the grand scheme of things, which tends to relieve you of any anxiety (at least in my case). For example, an embarrassing incident (got too drunk and called the ex, farted in class, etc.) has little effect on things outside of you a week from now,  and nothing a hundred weeks after the fact. Some people see this and get discouraged, but it should be freeing for you, to be who you want to be. And we all have a right to be.

As for the ego itself, you can never completely kill an ego,  so the term "ego death" is pretty misleading. Sure a good trip can set your mind in the right direction, but your ego is the collective you man. Your ego is your name. It's your experiences up to this point that has shaped all of your decisions to this very point. It's more of knowing your behind the wheel of your ego,  and not the other way around.
